clue.text: Missing articles — llamas confused with lamas — I've got plenty of tricks

indicators.note: confused tells us the remaining letters are jumbled into a new order
missing means the named letters are dropped from the two animal words

parts.note: A is the indefinite article, and two articles give two As

explanation.surface: Someone muddles South American pack animals with Tibetan monks and boasts of a trick-filled hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Missing articles' takes two As out of LLAMAS + LAMAS, leaving LLMSLAMAS; 'confused' rearranges those nine letters. In bridge the small slam is winning twelve of the thirteen tricks.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridge player who bids and makes a small slam takes twelve tricks, so the contract itself claims plenty of tricks.

clue.text: Russian girl is ashamed to part

indicators.note: to part means only a part of the words is ours, run across their middle

explanation.surface: A Russian girl is too embarrassed to say goodbye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to part' looks like separating, but it signals that the answer sits inside 'is ashamed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sasha is a common Russian girl's name, a pet form of Alexandra.

clue.text: Vitamin B for Bevan

explanation.surface: A vitamin pill is recommended for a Welsh politician.
explanation.walkthrough: Two definitions joined by 'for'. Aneurin Bevan was the Welsh Labour minister who founded Britain's National Health Service.
explanation.definitionFit: Aneurin is an old name for thiamine, vitamin B1, and was also the first name of the statesman Nye Bevan.

clue.text: 17 has left Kipling's grey wolf and doesn't start

parts.note: Akela is the grey wolf who leads the pack in Kipling's Jungle Book

indicators.note: doesn't start means the word and loses its opening letter

explanation.surface: A dog has abandoned the old wolf from The Jungle Book and refuses to get going.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 is TERRIER, so the definition is a breed of terrier. 'and' without its first letter gives ND.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lakeland is a breed of terrier from the Lake District of north-west England.

clue.text: See 3
Roman venue arranged for me darlin'

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of the two words are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A Roman meeting place is set up for a sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges ROMAN VENUE. The Irish endearment comes from mo mhuirnín, 'my darling'.
explanation.definitionFit: An Irish term of endearment meaning my darling, used in songs such as Kathleen Mavourneen.

clue.text: Deity some see as a tyrant

indicators.note: some means we take only some of the letters, a run inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Some people regard a god as a cruel ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' signals a run inside 'see as a tyrant'.
explanation.definitionFit: A satyr is a minor woodland god of Greek myth, half man and half goat.

clue.text: Boy's terror curtailed by drums

parts.note: Tim is a boy's name

indicators.note: curtailed means the word for terror loses its tail, its final letter

parts.note: panic is sudden terror

explanation.surface: A boy's fear is cut short by the sound of drums.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtailed' cuts the last letter off PANIC to give PANI.
explanation.definitionFit: Timpani are kettledrums, the large tuned drums of an orchestra.

clue.text: Top job topped — it's a hospital job

indicators.note: topped means the word loses its top, its first letter

parts.note: the presidency is the top job in a republic or company

explanation.surface: Losing the highest post lands someone a junior hospital post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topped' removes the first letter from PRESIDENCY.
explanation.definitionFit: A residency is the period of specialist training a doctor serves in a hospital.

clue.text: Expressive books that needn't be read

explanation.surface: Talking books are full of meaning even if no one opens them.
explanation.walkthrough: Two definitions: the idiom for being highly expressive, and a literal reading as books that talk, so no reading is required.
explanation.definitionFit: To say a great deal without words is the idiom's meaning; literally, volumes that speak are audiobooks.

clue.text: 27 17 exposed to drink

parts.note: laundry or opinions that are aired are exposed to the open
ale is a drink

explanation.surface: A Yorkshire dog has been left out in the open to have a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 27 is YORKSHIRE and 17 is TERRIER. 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Airedale is a large breed of terrier from the valley of the River Aire in Yorkshire.

clue.text: Drink time (two days) put on as extra

parts.note: to sup is to drink
an era is a period of time
D is the abbreviation for day, so two days give DD

explanation.surface: A drinking session lasting two days gets added on.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket hides that 'two days' is just two Ds.
explanation.definitionFit: To superadd is to add something over and above what is already there.

clue.text: 17 part of garden where heather's not raised

parts.note: a flower bed is part of a garden
ling is another name for heather

indicators.note: raised means turned upward, so in this down clue the word not is read bottom to top

explanation.surface: A dog's patch of garden is where the heather fails to grow tall.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 is TERRIER, so the definition names a terrier breed. 'raised' works because this is a down clue, where reading upwards turns a word round.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bedlington is a lamb-like breed of terrier from Northumberland in north-east England.

clue.text: M for a holiday?

parts.note: the letter M begins the name of the fifth month

explanation.surface: A single letter stands for a day off.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as wordplay: the first letter of MAY is M, which is the whole clue apart from the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: May Day, the first of May, is a traditional spring festival and a public holiday in many countries.

clue.text: Part of a 17, say, a beast of a weed

indicators.note: say tells us to go by how the terrier's name sounds rather than how it is spelt

parts.note: Dandie is the first part of the Dandie Dinmont, a breed of terrier
a lion is a beast

explanation.surface: A bit of a dog, so to speak, is a monster of a weed.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 is TERRIER. 'say' turns DANDIE into DANDE, which sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: The dandelion is a common yellow-flowered plant treated as a weed in lawns.

clue.text: Wear for station abroad among the sandhills

indicators.note: among puts the foreign station inside the word for sandhills

parts.note: dunes are sandhills
gare is French for a railway station

explanation.surface: Clothing for a posting overseas in the desert dunes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'station' reads as a posting, but here it is a railway station in French.
explanation.definitionFit: Dungarees are hard-wearing overalls, a garment one wears.

clue.text: 17 on high ground

explanation.surface: A dog stands on top of a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 is TERRIER, so one definition is a breed of terrier; the other describes a pile of stones as found on hilltops.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cairn is a small Scottish terrier; a cairn is also a heap of stones built as a marker on high ground.

clue.text: Lana Turner's head turned at birth

indicators.note: turned means these letters are turned about into a new order
the head of the word Turner's is its first letter

explanation.surface: The film star Lana Turner's head was turned when she was born.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' takes T from 'Turner's'; 'turned' rearranges LANA + T.
explanation.definitionFit: Natal means relating to birth, so it can stand for at birth, as in natal care.

clue.text: Row about slip up in the inventory

indicators.note: about means the row goes round the slip

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
to err is to slip up

explanation.surface: An argument breaks out over a mistake in the stock list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel but is a tier. 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrier is also a historical register or inventory of land and property, as held by a parish or estate.

clue.text: Say about Tracey being embraced by tinker, it appears

indicators.note: being embraced by means all that goes inside the tinker

parts.note: Christopher Sly is the drunken tinker in Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew

indicators.note: about puts the words for say round the artist's surname

parts.note: EG, for example, is what say means
Tracey Emin is the British artist

explanation.surface: Apparently Tracey has been hugged by a travelling tinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tinker' looks like a trade or a verb, but Araucaria means Shakespeare's tinker, Christopher Sly. 'about' and 'being embraced by' nest the pieces one inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Seemingly means apparently, which is what it appears does in a sentence.

clue.text: Roman brothers get fat keeping up numbered chariot

indicators.note: keeping means the fat holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: ghi, also spelt ghee, is clarified butter, a cooking fat

indicators.note: up means read upwards in this down clue, so the letters are turned round

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a number
a chariot is a car in old poetic usage

explanation.surface: Roman siblings are putting on weight while maintaining a numbered racing chariot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' works because this is a down clue, so the reversed letters RACC read upwards. 'get' is a link word, and 'fat' is the Indian cooking fat, also spelt ghee.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gracchi were Tiberius and Gaius Gracchus, brothers who were reforming tribunes of the Roman Republic.

clue.text: African currency comes in a little bit casually

indicators.note: comes in puts the currency inside the little bit

parts.note: an atom is a tiny bit
the rand is the currency of South Africa

explanation.surface: Some foreign money trickles in without any plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a little bit' reads as an amount but is ATOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something at random means doing it haphazardly, without method or plan.

clue.text: See 10
Little girl of the Spanish romance

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
a romance can be a fanciful invention or lie

explanation.surface: A young girl from a Spanish love story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'romance' suggests a love story but here means a made-up tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Ellie is a girl's name, a short form of Eleanor, so the definition is a girl in general.

clue.text: Group one can't make out

explanation.surface: A band whose words nobody can hear clearly.
explanation.walkthrough: Two definitions: Blur is a British rock band of the 1990s; a blur is a shape too indistinct to see.
explanation.definitionFit: Blur is a pop group, and a blur is something hazy that cannot be made out.

clue.text: Sure things

parts.note: plays on the saying as sure as these breakfast items are what they are, meaning certainties

explanation.surface: Certainties.
explanation.walkthrough: The old phrase 'as sure as eggs is eggs' means absolutely certain, so these are the things that are proverbially sure.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb makes them the standard of certainty, hence things that are sure.

clue.text: I'm at college: little work is required relative to how it's done

indicators.note: required is read as re-quired, the letters put together again in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
OP is short for opus, a work
taken as written

explanation.surface: A student reports that little effort is needed for the course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'required' rearranges I'M AT COLLEGE + OP + IS. Epistemology is the theory of knowledge, how knowing is done.
explanation.definitionFit: Epistemological means concerned with the theory of knowledge, the study of how knowing is carried out.

clue.text: Father's new hooter

parts.note: a sire is a father

explanation.surface: Dad has a new car horn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hooter' could be a nose or an owl; here it is a warning horn.
explanation.definitionFit: A siren is a device that makes a loud warning hoot.

clue.text: 17 to shirk problem in former days

indicators.note: in puts the rearranged letters inside the old times

parts.note: yore means times long past

indicators.note: problem treats the word shirk as a puzzle to be sorted out into a new order

explanation.surface: A dog dodging work was a problem back in the old days.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 is TERRIER, so the definition is the Yorkshire terrier. 'problem' rearranges the letters to KSHIR, and 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yorkshire terrier is a small long-haired breed, often called a Yorkie.
